# human-machine-swapper

> A dependency-free web component that adds a Human / Machine pill to any website, one file
> of about 6 KB gzipped. Machine
> shows the site's llms.txt, the plain-text reading written for language models, rendered in
> place without leaving the page. One script tag and one custom element, no build step.

## Install

    <script src="https://unpkg.com/human-machine-swapper" defer></script>
    <human-machine-swapper data-position="bottom-center"></human-machine-swapper>

Or: npm install human-machine-swapper

## Required, all three

1. Load the script (above), or import "human-machine-swapper".
2. Mount <human-machine-swapper> anywhere in <body>. It is position:fixed.
3. Add this CSS, which is NOT optional:

    human-machine-swapper:not(:defined) { display: none; }

Without step 3 the element is laid out in flow at about 50px tall until the script loads, and
pushes the rest of the page down.

## The site must have an llms.txt

The component renders nothing if it cannot find one, and writes a console warning explaining
how to publish one. Write the llms.txt first, or the change will look broken.

Point at it so the component does not have to probe for it:

    <link rel="llms" href="/llms.txt" />

## Options

data-position   bottom-center | top-center. Default bottom-center.
data-llms       auto | URL. auto reads link rel=llms, then probes /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt.
data-accent     CSS colour for the current dot and hover. Default #a8f326.
data-labels-human, data-labels-machine   Override the two labels.

## Behaviour

- Machine renders the file in place, over the page, with the pill still on screen. Human,
  Escape, and the browser back button all return the reader to the page.
- Machine is a real <a href> to the file: crawlers follow it, cmd-click and middle-click open
  the raw text in a new tab, and it works with JavaScript off. Only an unmodified left click is
  upgraded to the in-page reader.
- The component adds nothing to the host page's content and removes nothing from it.
- The pill renders in a shadow root, so it cannot collide with the host site's CSS.

## Key facts

Q: What is human-machine-swapper?
A: An Apache-2.0 web component published by Advance Labs Inc. that puts a Human / Machine
toggle on a website, where Machine shows the site's llms.txt rendered in place.

Q: How do I add a human machine toggle to a website?
A: Add the script tag, add the <human-machine-swapper> element, add the
human-machine-swapper:not(:defined){display:none} CSS rule, and make sure the site serves an
llms.txt.

Q: Why is the pill not showing up?
A: Almost always because the site has no llms.txt. The component hides itself when it has
nothing to switch to. Check the browser console for the warning.

Q: Does it put a badge on my site?
A: No. There is no visible credit on the host page. The reader's own header says "rendered by
Advance Labs", and a schema.org WebApplication node is added to the head.

Q: Does it work without JavaScript?
A: The pill needs JavaScript to render. The llms.txt it points at is a plain file at a stable
URL, so nothing is lost for crawlers.
